prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1249; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The front bumper cover is cracked across the center and the upper radiator support is bent, with the hood latch and both headlamp assemblies broken away from their mounts. The damage pattern lines up well with a frontal impact at low speed, and nothing I found points to older damage on the vehicle. The repair plan calls for replacing the bumper cover, radiator support, hood latch, and headlamps, followed by a realignment of the hood and fender gaps and a refinish of the front end. The labor hours requested match what this kind of work normally takes. The invoices submitted show each part and operation billed once, with no repeated charges.
